itemList.itemName: Daily rituals associated with the temple festival
On the day following the opening of the doors, carrying out the decoration of the Goddess and attending to other related tasks.

On the day the temple doors open, erecting coconut-frond pandals for the temple and the temple kitchen, and providing remuneration to the flower-stringers who craft the elaborate floral hair braids (moggu-jade)
Honorarium for those who sweep the temple premises, smear the entrance with cow-dung paste, draw Rangoli, and hang mango-leaf festoons.
Floral decoration for the palanquin (carrying the jewelry casket)
For designated tasks (whitewashing, pounding lentils, etc.)
For the Goddesss decoration  Abhisheka (ritual bathing) worship and Naivedya over a period of 13 days
Distribution of Prasada to Brahmins and Madivalas (washermen) when visiting the tank to wash the Goddesss garments Matte (ritual bundle of deitys ornaments) worship and Naivedya
For Pada Puja(worship of the deitys feet) and Naivedya at the Devigere(temple tank) and honorarium for the Addekara(ritual assistants)
Whitewashing the temple kitchen, sanctum sanctorum, and inner precincts
For the headgear (Mogata) worn by the priests
Service performed for one week starting from the day the doors close (Saptaha Seva)
Naivedya (food offering) provided from the day the doors open until they close
Service performed on Padyami (the first day of the lunar month)
Honorarium for Suhasinis (married women) on the day following the opening of the temple doors
